questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past?
options: I have lost my keys yesterday.
I have lost my keys.
I lost my keys yesterday.
I had lost my keys.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form to complete the sentence: "This movie is _______ than the one I saw last week."
options: more interesting
more more interesting
interestinger
most interesting

questions.question: Which option correctly uses the second conditional to talk about an unreal present situation?
options: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
If I know the answer, I will tell you.
If I knew the answer, I will tell you.
If I know the answer, I would tell you.
questions.answer: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a gerund after the verb 'enjoy'.
options: I enjoy swimming in the lake.
I enjoy to swim in the lake.
I enjoy swimming at the lake.
I enjoy swim in the lake.
questions.answer: I enjoy swimming in the lake.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the modal verb 'must' to express a strong deduction?
options: She must be at home; she is not answering the phone.
She must be at home; she is answering the phone.
She must have been at home; she is not answering the phone.
She must have been at home; she is answering the phone.
questions.answer: She must be at home; she is not answering the phone.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct linker to show contrast: "______ it was raining heavily, we decided to go for a walk."
options: Because
Although
So
And

questions.question: Which sentence uses the past continuous correctly to describe an action that was interrupted?
options: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
I sleep when the phone rang.
I slept when the phone rang.
I had slept when the phone rang.
questions.answer: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the infinitive after the verb 'want'.
options: I want go to the cinema.
I want to go to the cinema.
I want going to the cinema.
I want go to the cinema.
questions.answer: I want to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Which option correctly uses the comparative structure for a short adjective?
options: This car is faster than that one.
This car is more fast than that one.
This car is fastest than that one.
This car is faster than that one.
questions.answer: This car is faster than that one.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the third conditional to describe a past unreal situation.
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I will pass the exam.
If I studied harder, I would pass the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
